elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1: "each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed..." — the cap runs to both Parties symmetrically, and the deterministic check confirms no residual unlimited-Customer-liability language.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1: "the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000" — correct basis (paid or payable, not broader "all amounts"), correct 12-month lookback anchored to the claim, and the USD 1,000,000 floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 21.2: "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill" — already mutual and left untouched.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 defines Excluded Claims to include "a Party's breach of confidentiality... obligations"; deletion of "without exception" and insertion of "Except for Excluded Claims" in 21.1 now makes that carve-out operative against the cap.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "data-protection, or security obligations" within Excluded Claims, now excepted from the 21.1 cap.
21.3: "its indemnification obligations" within Excluded Claims, carved out of the re-based 21.1 cap.
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims, excepted in 21.1.
21.3: "wilful misconduct" within Excluded Claims; 21.1 now opens "Except for Excluded Claims".
21.3: "or fraud" within Excluded Claims; excepted from the cap by revised 21.1.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" within Excluded Claims, now genuinely outside the cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Revised 21.3: "Customer's payment obligations for undisputed amounts due under this Agreement, including Fees, taxes, expenses and interest, are not damages and are not limited by this Section." This resolves the defined-term trap in cl. 1.5 (Fees excludes taxes, reimbursable expenses, interest and implementation charges), so the carve-out reaches payment obligations as a whole rather than a narrow Fees subset.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 21.1: "Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" (with a USD 1,000,000 alternative floor), replacing the one-month walk-away basis.
Excluded Claims in 21.3 include indemnification obligations and are now excepted from 21.1.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims in 21.3 include breach of confidentiality obligations, operative via the new "Except for Excluded Claims" hook.
Excluded Claims in 21.3 include gross negligence.
Excluded Claims in 21.3 include wilful misconduct.

reasons: Deviation call is correct: original 21.1 capped both Parties at one month of Fees actually paid (below the 6-month walk-away floor) and the trailing "without exception" neutralised the entire Excluded Claims regime in 21.3, putting indemnities and confidentiality inside an illusory cap.
All eleven preferred elements are met in operative language; the level is position-complete, and the fallback is met a fortiori.

The edits are confined to the two defective mechanics: (i) the cap basis and the "without exception" override in 21.1, and (ii) the Customer-payment carve-out sentence in 21.3 whose reach was limited by the narrow cl. 1.5 definition of "Fees". Section 21.2, including the Customer-favourable direct-damages sentence, is untouched, and the "undisputed" qualifier is preserved.

Enumerating "Fees, taxes, expenses and interest" is close to surplus, but it is required to defeat the cl. 1.5 carve-out from "Fees" and so is tied to the selected element rather than being a free-standing extra; dropping "for conforming Services" is likewise necessary because the element requires coverage of payment obligations as a whole, not a subset. If the drafter wants a tighter edit, "Customer's payment obligations for undisputed amounts due under this Agreement" alone would carry the element.

Intent preserved: no dangling terms (Excluded Claims remains defined in 21.3), no contradictory retained sentence, and the mutual damages exclusion, direct-damages characterisation and Order Form fee mechanics survive unchanged.
Margin comment accurately states what changed and why and cites the playbook position; tone and prefix conform.
